summary: Customers' failed fund transfers are caused by payment-service's mTLS client certificate (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal) expiring at exactly 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z. From 12:15:27Z onward, every call to bank-partner-api fails the TLS handshake (alert 45, expired certificate) and payments are marked PENDING_RETRY instead of completing. The HTTP error-rate dashboard is green because these queued/acknowledged payments are not surfaced as 5xx; the true signals are bank_api_error_rate jumping 0.2%->100% and payment_success_rate collapsing 99%->~2.5% at the same moment. Resource metrics (CPU, memory, DB pool, restarts) and request throughput are normal, ruling out resource/capacity causes. The earlier timeout config change (11:20Z) and the settlement-service deploy (10:30Z) both predate onset and do not fit a TLS-cert error. This matches historical HIST-106 (client cert expiry, no renewal automation). Fix: issue/reload a valid client cert for payment-service and drain the PENDING_RETRY backlog; add certificate-expiry monitoring/automated rotation and an alert on bank_api_error_rate / payment_success_rate.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Expired mTLS client certificate in payment-service breaks bank-partner-api calls
ranked_hypotheses.statement: payment-service's client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal expired at 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z. All outbound mTLS calls to bank-partner-api now fail the handshake (TLS alert 45), so payments are acknowledged and marked PENDING_RETRY instead of completing. The HTTP error_rate panel stays green because these are handled/queued, not 5xx.

causal_chain.claim: cert expiry -> mTLS handshake to bank-partner-api rejected (alert 45)
rejections -> payments marked PENDING_RETRY rather than 5xx
PENDING_RETRY path bypasses HTTP 5xx metric -> error_rate panel stays green

assumptions: Renewing/replacing the client cert will restore bank-partner-api connectivity
bank-partner-api accepts a renewed cert from the same CA/CN

ranked_hypotheses.title: Bank partner API outage (dependency failure)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: bank-partner-api is itself failing, causing payment calls to fail.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Logs explicitly attribute the failure to OUR expired client certificate (alert 45, our client cert CN=... notAfter=...), and a server-side outage would not produce a client-cert expiry error with an exact notAfter matching the onset. We cannot see partner telemetry (F10) but the local error is self-explanatory.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Config change (bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000) triggered failures
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The 11:20Z timeout increase caused the payment failures.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The config change occurred ~55 minutes before onset; onset at 12:15Z coincides exactly with the cert notAfter. The failures are TLS certificate errors, not timeout errors, so the timeout change is not on the causal path.

ranked_hypotheses.title: settlement-service deploy v1.9.0 caused the incident
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The settlement CSV exporter deploy degraded payments.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Deploy was at 10:30Z (~2h before onset) and unrelated to payment-service's outbound mTLS to bank-partner-api; symptoms are cert-expiry specific.

facts.statement: mTLS handshakes from payment-service to bank-partner-api began being rejected at 12:15:27Z.
The expired client certificate's notAfter timestamp (2026-04-02T12:15:00Z) coincides exactly with the failure onset.
bank_api_error_rate rose from ~0.2% to 100% at onset while the HTTP error_rate panel stayed flat (~0.2%).
payment_success_rate fell from ~99% to ~2.5% at the same onset.
Resource metrics (cpu ~30%, memory ~55%, db_pool ~8, restarts 0) were stable; request_rate ~100 req/s.
Failures persisted to the latest data (13:58:39Z); 311 of 313 WARN/ERROR entries relate to the cert/PENDING_RETRY issue.
The only config change was bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000 at 11:20Z; the only deploy was settlement-service v1.9.0 at 10:30Z; neither aligns with onset.

timeline.event: settlement-service v1.9.0 deployed (CSV exporter) - unrelated to onset
payment-service config change bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000 - precedes onset by ~55 min
mTLS client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal reaches notAfter / expires
First payments marked PENDING_RETRY (mTLS handshake rejected)
First explicit 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45)' log line
Incident reported by support (payments failing, error_rate dashboard green)
Failures still ongoing at latest data

recommended_actions.action: Issue/renew the payment-service mTLS client certificate and reload it into the service (trusted by bank-partner-api).
recommended_actions.rationale: The expired cert (notAfter 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z) is blocking all bank-partner-api calls; renewal is the direct fix.

recommended_actions.action: After cert reload, drain/replay the backlog of payments marked PENDING_RETRY (171+ cert failures, 140 PENDING_RETRY).
recommended_actions.rationale: These queued payments represent customer fund transfers that never reached the partner.

recommended_actions.action: Add certificate-expiry monitoring and automated rotation for payment-service's outbound mTLS certs.
recommended_actions.rationale: Expiry was silent until it broke; HIST-106 had the same 'no renewal automation' root cause.

recommended_actions.action: Alert on bank_api_error_rate and payment_success_rate (not just HTTP 5xx error_rate), since queued/PENDING_RETRY failures bypass the 5xx panel.
recommended_actions.rationale: The green 5xx dashboard masked a 100% partner API failure and ~2.5% payment success.

recommended_actions.action: Review the 11:20Z timeout change and 10:30Z settlement deploy as coincidental, not causal; no rollback needed for them.
recommended_actions.rationale: Neither aligns with onset; ruling them out avoids unnecessary changes.

data_gaps: bank-partner-api has no telemetry; its status is only inferable through payment-service callers (log query for it returned not_found). Partner-side confirmation of cert rejection is unavailable.
No cert-management/rotation telemetry was available to confirm the literal renewal state or whether any renewal job exists for payments-client.orangeinvest.internal.
payment-service WARN/ERROR log results were truncated (313 matched, 40 returned); the full population was summarized via top_patterns counts rather than read in full.

findings.statement: payment-service ERROR logs from 12:15:27Z onward show mTLS handshake rejections to bank-partner-api and an expired client certificate.

findings.statement: The two dominant ERROR patterns (171 cert-expiry + 140 PENDING_RETRY) account for 311 of 313 WARN/ERROR entries; failures persist through the latest data at 13:58:39Z.
The expired client cert's notAfter is exactly 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z; failures begin immediately after (12:15:27Z first PENDING_RETRY).
payment-service HTTP error_rate metric stays flat (~0.18-0.32%) across the whole window, explaining the green dashboard.
bank_api_error_rate jumps from ~0.2% to 100% starting in the 12:10-12:20 bucket and stays at 100% through 13:50.
payment_success_rate collapses from ~99% to ~2.5% at the same onset, corroborating real customer-facing payment failures.
Resource/health metrics are normal and stable: request_rate ~100 req/s, cpu_pct ~30%, memory_pct ~55%, db_pool_in_use ~8, restarts 0 throughout.
Only one config change near onset: payment-service bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000 at 11:20:00Z, ~55 min BEFORE the failure onset.
Only deployment in scope is settlement-service v1.9.0 at 10:30:00Z (new CSV exporter); no payment-service deploy and no settlement-service config change.
bank-partner-api is an external dependency with no telemetry; payment-service is its only caller and observes it via its own logs.
The failure is a client-side certificate expiry: the alert is raised against OUR client cert named payments-client.orangeinvest.internal, not a server/partner-side cert.
payments are marked PENDING_RETRY rather than surfaced as HTTP 5xx, which is why the HTTP error_rate panel (5xx-based) stayed green while actual payment success dropped.
